svg.text: A visual guide to least squares, model fit, inference, and special explanatory variables

g.text: 1. From multivariate data to a fitted plane
Collect \(n\) observations with \(k\) explanatory variables and one response: \((x_{i1},
\ldots,x_{ik},y_i)\). • Inspect variables individually; use transformations such as LNFA
CE and LNINCOME when skewness and nonlinear patterns suggest them. • Use scatterplot mat
rices and correlation matrices to summarize pairwise relationships. • Fit the regression
plane \(\widehat y=b_0+b_1x_1+\cdots+b_kx_k\).
2. Least squares objective
Determine the coefficients that minimize the sum of squared differences between observed
and fitted responses.
3. Term life fitted regression plane
4. Matrix solution and estimator properties
Normal equations vs solution: \(\mathbf X'\mathbf X\mathbf b=\mathbf X'\mathbf y\) vs \(
\mathbf b=(\mathbf X'\mathbf X)^{-1}\mathbf X'\mathbf y\) • Unbiasedness vs precision: \
(\mathrm E\mathbf b=\boldsymbol\beta\) vs \(\mathrm{Var}\mathbf b=\sigma^2(\mathbf X'\ma
thbf X)^{-1}\) • F1–F4 vs F1–F5: Gauss–Markov gives minimum-variance unbiased linear est
imation vs normality additionally gives a normal distribution for \(\mathbf b\)
5. Term life ANOVA: variation in LNFACE
Regression SS: 328.47 • Error SS: 630.43 • Total SS: 958.90
6. Goodness-of-fit measures
7. Test whether one coefficient matters
State \(H_0:\beta_j=0\) against \(H_a:\beta_j\ne0\). • Compute \(se(b_j)\) from \(s\) an
d the corresponding diagonal element of \((\mathbf X'\mathbf X)^{-1}\). • Form \(t(b_j)=
b_j/se(b_j)\) with \(df=n-(k+1)\). • Reject \(H_0\) when \u007c\(t(b_j)\)\u007c exceeds
the appropriate \(t\)-critical value; as a rule of thumb at 5%, a magnitude above two in
dicates importance.
8. Extending the linear model
Binary variable vs continuous variable: a binary coefficient compares the alternative le
vel with its base level; a continuous coefficient is an expected change per unit change,
holding other variables fixed. • Transformation vs nonlinear regression function: \(x,
x^2,\ldots,x^p\) or \(\ln x\) can be explanatory variables while the model remains linea
r in its parameters. • Interaction vs additive effects: with \(x_3=x_1x_2\), \(\partial\
mathrm E y/\partial x_1=\beta_1+\beta_3x_2\), so the effect of one variable depends on t
he other. • Pairwise correlation vs partial correlation: an added variable plot controls
for other explanatory variables and can reveal a relationship different from the unadju
sted correlation.
9. Partial correlation from a t-ratio
\(r(y,x_j\mid\text{other }x)=\dfrac{t(b_j)}{\sqrt{t(b_j)^2+n-(k+1)}}\)
